If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in the mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in the early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in the late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect market correction pressure.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) across recent days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to the forecast in the mid-horizon to smooth out volatility.

If forecast exceeds true value by >2% in the first 5 days, reduce subsequent forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence with observed trend.

If true price dips below forecast by >1.5% in the last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in the next 5 days to correct for underestimation.
